home.bodySnippet: OSCA Replacement Index OSCA 2024 V1.0 Explore how exposed each Australian occupation may be to current AI tools. Search a role, compare approximate salary exposure, and see how the baseline score changes across occupations and industries. Read methodology FROZEN PUBLIC BETA DATASET V1 HOW TO USE THIS BETA These scores are directional estimates of task-level automation exposure. They do not predict layoffs, wages, hiring, or public policy outcomes, and they should not be treated as career advice on their own. methodology.heading: Methodology
methodology.snippet: BACK TO INDEX Methodology This public beta is designed to help general readers understand how exposed different occupations may be to current AI tools. It is a directional reference, not a prediction engine. WHAT THIS INDEX DOES It compares occupations on a shared scale, overlays approximate salary data, and shows where current AI tools could be economically meaningful under simple baseline assumptions. WHAT IT DOES NOT DO It does not forecast layoffs, career outcomes, labour demand, individual productivity, or policy decisions. It also does not measure the value of human judgment, care, or social trust outside the score framework. WHAT OSCA IS OSCA is the Occupation Standard Classification for Australia. It is maintained by the ABS and gives a standard code, title, and description for occupations across the Australian workforce. This beta uses all 1,156 OSCA occupations from the 2024 v1.0 release.
